title: Known incorrect SU(2)_2 braid oracle sigma-sublink shortcut

scope.question: Locate why the old specialized SU(2)_2 braid-closure oracle disagreed with the generic SU(2)_k fusion-path evaluator on the Yasui Figure 2 CP2(a=1) Tham 5.11 check, and make the bad oracle visibly unsafe for future use.
scope.claim_boundary: This note establishes a repo-local tool bug in the old specialized oracle. It does not claim a new mathematical formula, does not invalidate the n18b restricted no-crossing SU(2)_2 evaluator core, and does not by itself prove the Tham 5.11 upside-down interpretation.

repo_snapshot.dirty_status_summary: Pre-existing unrelated dirty CTL merge files were present. Yasui Figure 2 / Tham 5.11 artifacts and diagnostic scripts were also uncommitted at the time this note was written.

related_current_graph_node.important_distinction: The current graph node n18b refers to src/twisted_yetter/su2_link_evaluator.py at commit 137d449, a restricted bare no-crossing SU(2)_2 evaluator core. The bug recorded here is in the later experimental Sage braid oracle experiments/sage/su2_2_braid_oracle.sage.py, added at commit 00afe39.

do_not_use_for: Yasui Figure 2 or Figure 3 Tham 5.11 comparison checks
Omega expansion where any contributing fixed sector contains two or more sigma-labeled components
normative CTL evidence for arbitrary braid-closure RT values
still_historical_for: Understanding earlier stress tests that used this oracle only as an experimental comparator
Small controls that do not exercise the bad multi-component sigma shortcut

exact_fault_location.bad_computation_summary: The function selects all components labeled sigma, extracts a selected subbraid, evaluates Sage's Jones polynomial of that selected sigma sublink at zeta_16, and then multiplies by a scalar ((-1)^(number_of_sigma_components-1))*sqrt(2). This shortcut was treated as the fixed-label SU(2)_2 RT value of the sigma-colored sublink.
exact_fault_location.why_this_is_wrong: The selected-subbraid Jones-polynomial shortcut is not equivalent to the full SU(2)_2 RT quantum trace in the conventions used by the generic fusion-path evaluator once more than one component is sigma-colored. It loses convention-sensitive information for multi-component sigma sectors. The diagnostic mismatch is already visible at fixed simple-label sectors, before summing Omega coefficients.
not_the_primary_fault: The Yasui Figure 2 Tham 5.11 normalization D^-2 is not the cause of this oracle mismatch.
The R1-normalized Yasui braid payload is not the cause of the sector-level oracle mismatch.
The n18b restricted no-crossing evaluator core is not the code path being diagnosed here.

test_case.source: R1-normalized Yasui Figure 2 CP2(a=1) braid payload

reproduction.diagnostic_interpretation: Every displayed mismatch has exactly two sigma labels. This localizes the bad behavior to the sigma sublink Jones-polynomial shortcut, not to the Omega summation layer.

yasui_cp2_resolution.false_alarm: The old oracle made the Yasui Figure 2 CP2(a=1) D^-2 comparison appear to fail.
yasui_cp2_resolution.corrected_backend: Using experiments/sage/su2k_fusion_braid_evaluator.sage.py at level 2, with total framings rather than old extra-framing input, the R1-normalized Yasui raw value divided by D^2 matches the standard +1 framed Omega_0 unknot value.

additional_backend_checks.note: Generic SU(2)_k evaluator gave Yasui raw / D^2 equal to standard +1 Omega_0 unknot.
Floating generic SU(2)_k evaluator gave Yasui raw / D^2 equal to standard +1 Omega_0 unknot.
The selected SU(3)_2 convention matches untwisted and character rows; cat_1_3_2 does not match naively and remains a convention warning.

important_previous_warning.meaning: A previous artifact already avoided blocking Yasui payload admission on the legacy Jones diagnostic, but did not fully identify the oracle bug.
This artifact is now understood as contaminated by the bad old oracle convention and should not be used as evidence against the Tham 5.11 working interpretation.

triage_policy: Artifacts whose only role was stress-testing the old oracle should be treated as historical experimental evidence.

Artifacts that used the old oracle as an external comparator for an explicit R/F backend need fresh comparison against the generic SU(2)_k evaluator or another independent categorical implementation before admission.
Any future Yasui, Tham 5.11, or twisted-Yetter computation must not cite experiments/sage/su2_2_braid_oracle.sage.py as a normative backend.

source_changes_made_for_future_users.change: Add top-of-file known-incorrect/deprecated warning pointing to this lab note and the replacement generic SU(2)_k evaluator.
Add front-page warning that the README describes a historical oracle with a known multi-component sigma-sector bug.

next_actions: Do not delete the old oracle immediately, because older artifacts and scripts still need historical reproducibility.
For any local-piece or R/F backend artifact that used the old oracle only as a comparator, rerun the relevant comparisons against experiments/sage/su2k_fusion_braid_evaluator.sage.py at k=2.
When admitting future CTL claims, explicitly exclude the old oracle as normative evidence unless the claim is only about historical provenance.
